candidates/opt-davudk-terrain.title: Procedural World Generation
candidates/opt-davudk-terrain.content:
Procedural World Generation refinement
Source-screened 25 November 2026 at f7b1daa7a61af3ce9bf7e06fa77dfc4fcf89296c. MIT license, manifest, CPU terrain and carve routines, analytic height and channel profile, streamed globe tiles, globe sampling, network extraction, graph storage.
Promising permissive full formation alternative and geometry-realization donor. extractNetwork groups thresholded drainage cells into reaches and represents lake outlets and terminal lakes; GraphBuilder finalizes typed arrays. riverSegments and carveSegmentCpu rasterize channel/valley caps from segment geometry, with a parabolic profile in carveProfile. buildTileCpu combines coarse samples, deterministic noise, supplied river segments, bed/shore bounds and local thermal relaxation. These are specific existing routines that can be exercised independently of WebGL rendering, with narrow integration/port work. Reuse the tested parts with required notices, not the whole browser app.
Limitations: the macro network consumes coarse routing. Additional source inspection identified a real deterministic local creek generator, described below; it is not yet qualified as authoritative fine hydraulic topology. Streamed spherical tiles use margins and residency-dependent blends/fallbacks. The current sphere segment lookup iterates all tile buckets, so do not inherit that hot-path complexity. Flat detail is a dense 2048/4096 map; GPU and CPU paths differ. The profile uses supplied water levels and visual shoreline bounds, so separate immutable bank/bed geometry from live water stage before use. Its thermal pass clamps terrain and is not a conservative live sediment solver. Avoid a minimum channel width tied to coarse render texels. No finite water inventory, edited volumetric terrain or qualified Godot integration. No target-hardware measurement.
Qualification: compare source CPU routines against their native C++/Rust integration on a two-region anchored drainage fixture; preserve bankfull geometry and explicit terminal basins; test cold adjacent pages in opposite orders, partial residency, boundary samples and actual voxel/analytic profile agreement. Separately close regional tributary/outlet construction. No code has been incorporated.
Full generator and creek review
Pipeline order, erosion stages, stream-power solver, configuration, landforms, arid, karst, sea cliffs, hydrology. The actual pipeline builds plates, base relief, stamps, landscape evolution, macro refinement, climate, glacial landforms, other landforms, hydrology, biomes and landmarks. It explicitly generates terraced mesas/buttes/escarpments, coastal cliffs and sea stacks, dolines, towers and cenotes, volcanism, glacial/coastal formations and water features. The stream-power solver advances uplift/incision/diffusion over iterations with dt in years (250,000 years per iteration at the inspected stage). The top-level geologicAge is a 0–1 parameter influencing terrain characteristics and iteration settings. This is genuine numerical landscape evolution during staged generation, but not the same as GeoGenesis’s persistent multi-process geological time loop. Hydrology and climate are generation-time diagnostics, not a verified live finite weather/water cycle.
Correction to the initial refinement screen: creekGen.ts already supplies seeded D8 trunks and per-cell creek growth against a heightAt callback, an indexed segment representation, runoff-derived width/depth and connections to other channels, water or sinks. tests/creeks.test.ts contains order/batch consistency, terminal, monotonicity, no-crossing and performance assertions. These are source-inspected tests, not independently executed results. The manager selects visible cells/tier and caches ribbon graphs; the generator recomputes D8 receivers from macro elevations, permits sinks and has fallback joins. Its actual fine-path sampling depends on the supplied rendered height callback. For Breachborn replace that callback with stable authoritative geometry, test parent routing/closed-basin agreement and finite water ownership, and make the feature recipe independent of the camera. The existing local creek algorithm materially reduces the earlier presumed custom refinement gap but does not close it.
The headless benchmark harness directly invokes the pipeline without the viewer. Use that entry point for a bounded comparison before porting large TypeScript components. Existing demo quality and test assertions do not establish 4,000 km runtime performance or native integration. See formation comparison.

candidates/opt-geogenesis.title: GeoGenesis
candidates/opt-geogenesis.content:
GeoGenesis
Repository: github.com/nico2525nn/geogenesis ; prior research pin aa898282cbddc71a515deb58a0aa41f649e00147. Prior source inspection: flat fields and Simulation::new/step, no supplied C ABI. Single-shot age; tiled initial relief only. Export final original elevation, soil/geology/climate/receiver fields; refresh after aging. Diagnostic filled depth/discharge is not finite water. Author 256² 105 ms, 512² 420 ms, 1024² 1.82 s; 512² aging 65 ms per 10,000 modeled years; no Breachborn benchmark. Qualify on target hardware and actual geography. Core pilot, not mature turnkey engine.
Comparative formation review
Initial landforms, stratigraphy, chemical erosion, minerals, simulation driver. Initial relief contains plateaus, mesas, rifts, ranges, trenches, peaks and calderas; age advances coupled surface processes in physical years. Stratigraphic columns include rock properties, layer thickness, dip, fault displacement and age, potentially useful for native material queries. Mineral outputs score prospectivity and illustrative inventory, not 3D ore-body formation. Karst dissolution modifies surface elevations, not an underground tunnel network. Both initial and aged terrain are heightfields, not fully volumetric terrain.
The user finds the Procedural World Generation demo more compelling aesthetically. Reopen the surface-formation selection as a bounded comparison with OPT-DAVUDK-TERRAIN; GeoGenesis remains the existing provisional choice until selection evidence is obtained. See formation comparison. No source or runtime benchmark was executed.

candidates/opt-libmorton.content:
libmorton
MIT license, header. Exposes inline 2D/3D 32-bit and 64-bit Morton encode/decode, with compile-time instruction-set branches and portable alternatives. Qualify actual CPU feature dispatch and ARM portability before adoption. No benchmark.

MAIForge regional terrain
Source-screened at cc30cd7bfbb217acca590c4f2ea0cc6aa34b8084. README, pf-region license/manifest, regional module, skeleton, seam-certificate exploration.
Native Rust project builds a chart-wide drainage skeleton constrained to coarse receiver/outlet basins, regional relief windows and fine tiles. The skeleton distinguishes terminal segments, coarse edges and headwater extensions. Its experimental seam module uses fixed drainage/sea/lake seeds rather than treating arbitrary tile edges as outlets, and marks fills or donor dependencies contaminated by the window boundary. This is a directly relevant research question for independently generated regions. The project’s own README says its example fails strict drainage/coast/mean-height quality checks. It is not a finished replacement, and the region crate explicitly uses AGPL-3.0-only. Alternative licensing is mentioned by the project but not granted to us. Do not incorporate its code; evaluate published algorithms independently and use only as a conceptual comparison unless a compatible license is actually obtained. No benchmark performed.

candidates/opt-overlandflow.title: Landlab OverlandFlow
candidates/opt-overlandflow.content:
Landlab OverlandFlow
Source inspection 25 November 2026. Landlab pin 2e2c16093afb24093b7d75c577dad519423f23d3; component, license, method documentation, validation paper.
Actual capability: de Almeida local-inertial shallow-water approximation. It reads grid node bed/depth, link discharge, Manning roughness and water-surface gradients, computes face discharge and updates depth by rainfall minus flux divergence. Adaptive stability interval depends on grid spacing and maximum depth. Useful bounded fine/reference model for lake-at-rest, backwater, wetting and draining and signed head-driven flows.
Critical qualification: Constructor adds h_init water to node depths; the steep-slope branch floors low depths after updates. These are not acceptable unaccounted sources in a finite game inventory. The Python/NumPy raster grid is not a subgrid storage-curve solver. Need explicit face width/discharge units (documentation and source conventions must be checked), physical boundary conditions, donor limits, and actual accepted volume conservation. No direct runtime adoption or blanket per-metre flood solving. Use as an independent numerical reference or evaluate extraction of narrow MIT kernels only after proof. No candidate benchmark run.

candidates/opt-river-tree.title: Hydrological construction trees
candidates/opt-river-tree.content:
Hydrological construction trees
Primary publication: doi.org/10.1145/2461912.2461996 . The abstract establishes a geometric drainage graph, watershed classification and analytic feature-composition tree with carving/blending and varying visual LOD. This is the relevant shape of an age-preserving refinement method: constrain a region’s outlets and river graph, then synthesize land around those features. It does not establish finite water or runtime edits, and no licensed author implementation has been qualified.
A third-party implementation was inspected at github.com/bmelaiths/terrainHydrology/tree/09366289a002e7b58290b0cbd76c5b241c7cbfe6 . Its src/hydrology.py is a Python raster-export program using NumPy/SciPy, NetworkX, OpenCV, Shapely and Rasterio. README excludes inland lakes and the pinned tree has no root reuse license. Do not copy this implementation. Treat paper methods as research and seek a permissive reusable kernel, not a ready-made dependency. No benchmark run.

Source inspection 25 November 2026. Pin 5a6c0866d773169dcb5be73e006bfb475b31e859; manifest, library API, hydrology, C ABI, builder. Core license declaration Apache-2.0; default-features=false retains noise =0.9.0. Verify transitive licenses before incorporation.
Actual capability: Flat row-major Grid buffers, deterministic D8 accumulation and Priority-Flood with a separate filled height field, ocean connectivity from map boundaries, river/lake masks, optional droplet erosion and basin breaching. The C ABI already exposes an opaque terrain owner, ABI/version/status checks and borrowed read-only layer pointers; useful model for a GeoGenesis adapter.
Limitation: The public builder generates its own normalized dense heightmap, rather than accepting an existing aged coarse field and explicit tile-boundary constraints. Hydrology is a private module; no public receiver graph or elevation-in-metres runtime handoff. The flood-fill assumes finite map boundaries are outlets, ordering of f32 bit patterns assumes nonnegative heights, every cell adds one unit of rainfall, and filled depressions are geometry masks rather than finite lakes. Whole-map sort/heap/arrays and droplet aging do not prove bounded refinement. Do not substitute it for GeoGenesis or call it independently on tiles.
Next: Determine whether its small permissive routing/geometry functions can be isolated with explicit supplied outlet/saddle constraints and original bed preserved; compare against other permissive Priority-Flood donors. Source inspected, not built or benchmarked.

candidates/opt-tiled-priority-flood.content:
Tiled Priority-Flood
Primary paper: doi.org/10.1016/j.cageo.2016.07.001 . The tiled method bounds tile access/communication count, but still processes all supplied cells. It is a geometry/routing preparation reference, not a finite flood simulator, arbitrary incremental topology repair or instant global fine-world solution. The author reports a 2 trillion-cell run taking 4.8 h with 48 cores, not a game-scale performance result.
Reference repo: github.com/r-barnes/Barnes2016-ParallelPriorityFlood/tree/b6a91388ad044b49ae05bfbfe2d36b47e9159040 . Pinned .gitmodules points to RichDEM; earlier research found GPL-3.0 on the RichDEM dependency. The archive has no verified standalone permissive dependency chain. Do not embed as-is. Extract the conceptual boundary-summary approach independently only if justified; seek a permissive implementation before writing a solver.

candidates/opt-troute-diffusive.title: NOAA t-route diffusive routing
candidates/opt-troute-diffusive.content:
NOAA t-route diffusive routing
Source inspection 25 November 2026. Pin 12a8eae0cdfed437143c590659fa7077605a5e70; C binding, solver, cross-section tables, license.
Actual capability: c_diffnw bind(c) accepts caller arrays for reach network, geometry, lateral and boundary hydrographs, initial discharge and outputs discharge/elevation/depth over evaluation time. Solver uses Crank-Nicolson/Hermite interpolation and Fortran module-global allocatables. Cross-section generator handles compound synthetic or irregular bathymetric cross sections with stage-dependent hydraulic quantities and conveyance tables.
Limit: The ABI wraps a complete network interval, not an independently callable per-edge flux or a reentrant persistent basin owner. Mutable module globals and dense reach/component/time arrays need explicit ownership and memory qualification. No demonstrated finite ocean, arbitrary dams/sparse topology repair or connected 2D subgrid inundation. Do not resurrect the failed CaMa transplant by changing the library name. Prefer evaluating the independently callable cross-section table calculation or its permitted numerical routines as a donor; compare against geometry reference for stage-volume/area, not as proof of routing. No build or benchmark performed.

contracts/con-lod.title: Spatial levels and ownership transfers
contracts/con-lod.content:
Spatial levels and ownership transfers
Define per domain: stable spatial key, authoritative resolution, summary resolution, detail residency reason, temporal cadence, promotion/restriction, error bounds, cache size and invalidation. Never assume single uniform grid. Parent summaries are not duplicate child owners. For fine terrain, deterministic reconstruction plus edit overlay; for water, conservative partition of finite stores; for entities, retained individual IDs and aggregate event accounting. Camera requests rendering only, simulation can request detail offscreen.
Quantitative pilot
Use DEC-SPATIAL-PILOT to compare shared spatial indexing and separate field authority. Qualification plan defines the discriminating tests. Do not choose a global dense metre/250 m representation just to simplify coupling.
Concrete provisional pilot
Spatial architecture selection: shared metric coordinates, compact 16 km region directory, dense coarse fields, optional domain-specific payloads, persistent geometry features and independent Zylann fine blocks. Region addresses are not solver ownership or simulation cadence. Use stable IDs and revisioned derived data, no universal octree. Record exact partial-cell areas and wrapped seam rules. Coarse geometry/physics continue without voxel viewer admission. Test no fine-world allocation and bounded activity-dependent residency.

contracts/con-nav.title: Navigation truth and abstraction
contracts/con-nav.content:
Navigation truth and abstraction
Regional portals, connectivity and travel costs derived from terrain/material/clearance, access and hazards. Stable spatial IDs and revision dependencies. Long routes are high-level waypoints/segments with bounded refined queries; no dense metre corridor. Distinguish unknown, pending, stale, proven blocked, valid and approximate. On terrain/flood changes invalidate affected routes; broad connectivity changes may propagate. Offscreen travel shares timing/capacity and validates consequential transitions. Exact local motion checks current proof. Measure path error, search/rebuild time, memory and throughput.
Spatial pilot interface
Spatial architecture selection uses common metric region identities, not the render tree. Global and regional passage summaries must not require all descendants’ fine leaves to be resident or generated before planning; mark uncertain paths and refine consequential crossings. Existing exact remote segment proof is a historical implementation rule, not a new target restriction. Preserve edit/flood invalidation, time and capacity. Navigation library selection is separate.

contracts/con-terrain.title: Terrain authority and granularity
contracts/con-terrain.content:
Terrain authority and granularity
Proposed authority: generation produces immutable versioned macro fields and constrained fine recipe; terrain owner resolves current solid geometry/material from that recipe plus committed edits. Zylann provisional owner of current voxel data. A macro field is not a complete fine occupancy truth; a rendered mesh never becomes authority. Coarse summaries derive from actual recipe/edits; dirty bounds/revisions invalidate relevant geometry consumers. Store seed, model version, dimensions, edit overlay; do not allocate dense metre grids. X/Z/Y-up, metre SDF existing convention; exact target lattice open.
Refinement geometry boundary
Spatial architecture selection proposes a single aged baseline with region-crossing constraints, stable channel/bank profiles, terminal basin geometry and deterministic fine evaluation. The MIT donor may help realize geometry but not choose all tributary topology. Current river stage must never recarve the bed by changing the generator input. Current edits override the generated baseline and invalidate dependent summaries; use exact local SDF only where necessary, not as routine coarse hydraulic geometry derivation.
Volumetric geology qualification
Neither formation candidate supplies a complete editable volumetric world. Surface geometry is a heightfield; use the same canonical aged baseline plus sparse deterministic Zylann SDF features and committed edits for caves, overhangs and tunnels. Material identity must be coherent in X/Y/Z (strata, physical properties, finite mineable deposits), not inferred from a rendered biome color. Underground openings, aquifer/cave connectivity and flood barriers require actual shared geometry; ordinary surface queries must not materialize unrelated underground voxels. See Q-VOLUME and formation comparison.

contracts/con-water.title: Water inventory and hydraulic scale
contracts/con-water.content:
Water inventory and hydraulic scale
Use physical units: volume m³, stage m, discharge m³/s, velocity m/s, conserved mass/constituent kg or explicit units. Candidate storage relation V(h) monotonic; topology and connection curves revisioned from shared geometry. Finite donors, equal opposite transfers, pending rain/transit, ocean and groundwater inventories. Simultaneous outflows cannot overspend. Coarse/fine promotion partitions water, restriction sums. Local visual queries may approximate depth from connected surface; no independent water plane inventory. Accuracy tests include arrival, level, inundation and conservation, not ledger alone.
Geometry input distinction
Spatial architecture selection proposes deriving most bed, barrier, cross-section and storage descriptors from shared region/feature geometry, rather than repeated SDF scanning. One region may contain multiple disconnected finite stores. Do not use the coarse formation diagnostic lake level, donor’s visual water height or render residency as live volume authority. Topology change can propagate outside a local edited region; keep actual volume and constituent accounting during repair.

Git-native second brain

decisions/dec-formation.title: Formation and runtime separation
decisions/dec-formation.content:
Formation and runtime separation
GeoGenesis’s single-shot connected world can age; its tiled fast initial-relief path is not an aged-world refinement algorithm. Use coarse formation first; investigate hydrologically constrained refinement. Runtime land/water/atmosphere supply actual fluxes to periodic erosion. Import original final geography and freshly computed drainage, not diagnostic discharge as finite inventory. Exact grid and algorithms remain unresolved.
Formation comparison reopened
Source review shows Procedural World Generation is a genuine alternative for full staged surface formation, not merely a visual detail donor. Recommend testing it first for landform variety, linked drainage and refinement, with GeoGenesis as the existing provisional choice and stronger geological-age/material contender. Neither is a complete volumetric world or live environmental solver. Select exactly one baseline authority after the comparative gate in formation comparison. Borrow independently useful kernels/data adapters from the other only when justified; do not run two complete formation pipelines over the same world. No final change of accepted technology or implementation status.

decisions/dec-spatial-pilot.title: Spatial hierarchy qualification direction
decisions/dec-spatial-pilot.content:
Spatial hierarchy qualification direction
Hypothesis, not final selection
Use one coordinate and spatial identity convention, not a universal physical grid. Test a global coarse macro image and spatial index, sparse or compact regional features/pages, deterministic fine terrain, and domain-specific solvers. Start with 4 km macro candidates for the 4,000 km world and compare 1 km and 250 m land/refinement levels. At 256 km, compare the same physical scales and a denser macro source where worthwhile. Do not prescribe all-domain level sizes until actual kernel qualification.
Memory sizing
Illustrative 64 bytes per horizontal cell across a candidate packed field set. This is not measured implementation memory or a claim every field fits. Counts use ceiling division for complete square coverage. Excludes vertical layers, graph links, caches, edits, topology, scratch, snapshots and saves.




































































Spacing (m)256 km cell count64 B/cell4,000 km cell count64 B/cell40004,096256.00 KiB1,000,00061.04 MiB200016,3841.00 MiB4,000,000244.14 MiB100065,5364.00 MiB16,000,000976.56 MiB500262,14416.00 MiB64,000,0003.81 GiB2501,048,57664.00 MiB256,000,00015.26 GiB1006,553,600400.00 MiB1,600,000,00095.37 GiB10655,360,00039.06 GiB160,000,000,0009.31 TiB165,536,000,0003.81 TiB16,000,000,000,000931.32 TiB
A dense 250 m field set across 4,000 km would exceed 15 GiB before any other systems. Dense 1 km costs about 977 MiB even at only 64 B/cell. A 4 km global field is about 61 MiB. This is the reason to avoid hard-coding one resolution for every process. It does not forbid compact, compressed or sparse finer fields with proven budgets.
A 16 km regional page at 250 m contains 4096 cells, costing 256 KiB at 64 B/cell. 1024 such pages cost 256 MiB for that field set, covering 262,144 km², not the whole 4,000 km world. Pages with permanent edits or active storage must remain durably represented even when not resident. Use these values as workload probes, not fixed allocation targets.
Ownership by domain























































DataCandidate authoritative representationDerived consumersGeological baselineVersioned aged macro fields and deterministic regional recipeTerrain, materials, land hydrology, climate priorsSolid geometryFine procedural recipe constrained by durable features, plus committed edits, including cave and structure topologyMesh/collision, storage/face curves, navigation portalsClimate and weatherCoarse horizontal cells and optional vertical state, with conservative exchangesClouds, runoff, radiation, vegetation, wind effectsSoil/landPacked active land/catchment units; optional subgrid cover/soil partitionsRunoff, recharge, evapotranspiration, agricultureRivers/lakes/floodsConnected finite volume stores and geometry-dependent stage/flux relationships; distinct subgrid channels/basinsLocal level/depth/current, navigation hazards, erosionErosionMaterial and sediment budgets plus accepted terrain transactions; aggregate time-integrated forcingsUpdated geography and derived topologyVegetationPersistent cohorts/coverage and durable individual deltas when relevantHarvest, root effects, ET, habitatNavigationVersioned coarse region/portal connectivity and local refined evidenceRoutes, travel times and crowd motionPeople/itemsECS individual identities, finite item/needs state; shared batched activitiesLocal actors and offscreen outcomes
Coarse geometry is not exact fine solid truth; refinement must agree with explicit drainage and passage constraints. A coarse water store can represent many fine locations, but distinct sealed basins cannot share one undifferentiated water level. Use partitions or connectivity-aware features. An aggregate is not a second owner: promote by partitioning amounts and restrict by summing, with appropriate clocks and deterministic/validated reconstruction.
Clock and work scaling
A full linear pass over 16 million 1 km cells every simulated second costs 0.4 CPU seconds/game-second even at an optimistic 25 ns/cell, already 16x the historical 25 ms environment target. For one million 4 km cells the same hypothetical pass costs 25 ms. These are arithmetic examples, not measured performance. Use process-specific intervals, event/due work, compact field layouts and a complete inclusive budget. A severe island-wide storm must not force a fine-cell update everywhere.
First experiment
Use the qualification plan. Compare candidate costs at both world sizes and demonstrate preserved narrow channels and causal offscreen flooding. Final selection requires a measured connected implementation; no runtime launch is authorized by this document.
Source-screened selection update (25 November 2026)
Spatial architecture selection selects a simple global macro field + 16 km regional directory + sparse feature geometry + existing Zylann fine voxel residency for the pilot. The 1 km (256 km world) and approximately 4 km (4,000 km world) macro levels and 250 m regional resolution are comparison settings, not globally imposed. Prioritize the MIT Procedural World Generation donor for CPU channel/valley realization. Regional tributary topology and closed-basin reconciliation are still unresolved. Do not install a second voxel tree or generic AMR runtime. This is a provisional engineering selection; source inspected, not executed or accepted.
Formation review supplement
The same spatial hierarchy can consume either candidate’s exported geography. Formation comparison reopens the macro generator selection and identifies existing deterministic creek growth in Procedural World Generation. No universal grid or second terrain authority is introduced.

formation-comparison.title: World formation comparison and remaining terrain scope
formation-comparison.content:
World formation comparison and remaining terrain scope
Source review: 25 November 2026. Both candidates MIT. Existing provisional GeoGenesis selection remains subject to comparison; recommend Procedural World Generation first in the surface-formation comparison because the user values the demonstrated geographic quality. Neither is validated on target hardware. No engine code modified.
Actual scope























































CapabilityGeoGenesisProcedural World GenerationSurface geographyTectonic relief, crust/isostasy, landform stamps and ageTectonic relief, staged landform passes, LEM and refined terrainGeological timePersistent coupled simulation, age in years, replayIterated uplift/incision/diffusion with time step in years; age-conditioned parameters, staged buildReliefPlateaus, mesas, ranges, rifts, faults, calderas, peaksTerraces, mesas, buttes, escarpments, coastal cliffs, sea stacks, volcanism, karst and glacial/coastal landformsGeology/materialsRock properties, strata, age, dip, fault offset, soil/sediment, mineral prospectivityErodibility, geological provinces, simplified strata/landform and biome layersDrainageD8/MFD, depression fill, climate-derived flow; needs finer realizationExplicit reach graph, lakes, meanders, deltas, local trunk/creek growth and CPU terrain detailOutputHeightfield, maps, 3D surface mesh, geology descriptorsHeightfield, typed-array fields, feature graphs, CDLOD surface and visual effectsTrue volumetric terrainNot suppliedNot suppliedLive finite gameplay hydrology/weatherNot suppliedNot suppliedNative integrationDependency-light Rust core, export/ABI adapter neededTypeScript numerical core and headless benchmark; export/native port of proven functions to qualify
GeoGenesis source: initial formation, age driver, geology, mineral scoring. PWG source: pipeline, LEM, age config, landforms, arid, cliffs, hydrology, creeks, creek tests.
Recommendation: compare whole formation outputs, not stack two full generators. PWG’s explicit landform diversity and local creek implementation may avoid significant custom engineering. GeoGenesis is better aligned with chronological coupled age and material inventories. A beautiful demo does not by itself establish native runtime speed, physically correct finite water, or 3D geology. PWG’s rendering and visual embellishment should not be mistaken for the physical terrain. If PWG wins, consider only needed compatible GeoGenesis rock/stratigraphy and geological-process kernels, not a second world owner. If GeoGenesis wins, borrow PWG’s targeted landform/creek/geometry routines rather than running PWG’s entire macro pipeline afterward.
Bounded selection gate

Run both pinned upstream generators headlessly using the same physical world width and comparable output resolution/land fraction/climate settings. Use a small reproducible seed set representing humid mountainous islands, dry plateau/canyon terrain and volcanic or glacial terrain. Seeds need not map to identical geography across different algorithms. Inspect final exported elevation, not renderer exaggeration, and measure cold macro generation, aging/evolution, refinement/export and peak working memory separately. GeoGenesis’s author timings are not a direct comparison; PWG has a source-inspected benchmark entry point.
Compare actual plateau/cliff profiles, river continuity, lake/outlet connectivity, relief variation, geology/material information, age controls and age-dependent changes. Freeze tolerances and visual evaluation views before testing. Report which landforms are process-driven vs explicit stamps; both are legitimate if coherent and configurable.
Test actual natural fine river/creek realization, including 1 m feature geometry where representable, cross-page continuity, closed basins, deterministic re-generation and no view-dependent physical geometry. Existing creek tests are useful starting evidence, not our validation. A fixed height callback and persistent parent routing/finite inventory contracts are mandatory.
Only after upstream evidence, compare native interop costs and one bounded Godot/Zylann view with true caves and materials. Select one source. Do not start a large port or new framework to make either candidate fit. Probe 4,000 km coarse scaling with no dense fine allocations. Distinguish failed/partial/accepted results.

Additional scope retained from the environmental plan
These items are not made unnecessary by selecting a formation engine. They remain required or explicitly phased in existing records.

questions/q-flood.title: Which scalable hydraulic algorithm?
questions/q-flood.content:
Which scalable hydraulic algorithm?
Qualify signed head law, wet/dry, backwater, control/levee, downstream arrival, storage curves and dynamic geometry. Compare whole-island storm and two-basin/levee cases against finer reference with declared error and memory/throughput. No wholesale local refinement. Use historical SWMM/CaMa failures as negative evidence.
Numerical source screen
Landlab OverlandFlow is an independently implemented local-inertial raster reference. NOAA t-route diffusive routing exposes a C binding and cross-section preparation; the whole solver has module-global state. Neither qualifies as a turnkey sparse subgrid engine. Compare two practical coarse algorithms: a signed quasi-steady diffusive-wave head law using stage-dependent conductance versus a local-inertial face-discharge update retaining prior momentum. Use SFINCS/CaMa as algorithm references and independent fine Landlab controls. Start with one conservative stage-volume store per connected partition and explicit saddle/face geometry; both alternatives must handle closed barriers and exact accepted-volume debit/credit. Reject equilibrium-only flow for travel-time tests, unaccounted thin films/floors, or a requirement to promote an entire storm region to metre cells. See spatial qualification. This is a shortlist for tests, not a selected production solver.

questions/q-refine.title: How to refine aged geography?
questions/q-refine.content:
How to refine aged geography?
Smallest decisive experiment: age a coarse seed, generate adjacent fine regions and a shared creek/lake; compare drainage/outlet continuity, slope/section geometry, seam determinism, memory and startup. Inspect reusable hydrological terrain generation, graph/drainage algorithms and licenses. Tiled initial relief is not sufficient.
Narrowed research
Hydrological construction trees and procedural planet refinement are promising methods, not qualified licensed implementations. Tiled Priority-Flood addresses geometry reconciliation, not finite runtime water. flowing-terrain is a small permissive candidate with a closed-basin limitation. Neural Earth provides corroborating architecture, not a selected dependency. Test a constrained coarse/fine seam before committing to one method. See qualification plan.
Additional native donor screen
terrain-generator exposes a compact Apache-2.0 Rust/C interface and deterministic dense-map hydrology. Its bounded-map border-outlet policy, normalized heights, private flow functions and absent parent-boundary refinement prevent selection as an aged refinement engine. Investigate narrow geometry primitives only if they materially reduce new integration code.
Preferred source-screened geometry donor
Procedural World Generation is a promising MIT CPU routine donor for constrained channel and valley geometry from coarse fields. Qualify supplied-feature realization first. It cannot yet be called an aged geographic refinement engine because it does not guarantee new tributary/outlet topology; the remaining question is regional drainage construction and cross-window reconciliation. MAIForge has relevant pinned-outlet/window methods but AGPL and its own failed strict quality checks; reference only. Spatial architecture selection describes the bounded pilot.
Correction and comparative gate
Additional pinned source inspection located the deterministic per-cell trunk/creek generator and its tests within Procedural World Generation. It supplies an actual reusable topology lead, not only carving. It currently feeds visible river ribbons and samples a supplied rendered height callback, so the authoritative, camera-independent topology/bed and finite-store handoff still need qualification. See candidate record and formation comparison.

questions/q-volume.title: How to generate coherent volumetric geology?
questions/q-volume.content:
How to generate coherent volumetric geology?
Separate procedural surface generation from volumetric detail. Zylann’s existing VoxelGeneratorGraph supports SDF composition and caves (documentation, generators). Use age/geology and material features to control cave topology, cliff overhangs, fractures and ore placement, not random unrelated noise everywhere. GeoGenesis stratigraphic/prospectivity outputs may be useful inputs, not proven 3D resource deposits. Investigate existing reusable volumetric generation examples/kernels and retain only relevant proven features. Test a connected cave and surface entrance, a true overhang, stratigraphic section and finite mineable deposit across neighboring blocks and restart; demonstrate that an edit changes both liquid storage/connectivity and navigation summaries without dense volume initialization. No implementation selected for these geological semantics. See formation comparison.

Extreme efficiency and adverse workloads
Reference Ryzen 7 3700X, RTX 2070 SUPER, 32 GB. Initial desired 8x rendered, future 32–64x; ~25 CPU-ms/game-second environmental target, old 512 MiB steady/768 MiB autosave/1 GiB transient, water 32 MiB VRAM, 0.5 ms GPU/frame and 0.3 ms main handoff are starting targets, not immutable allocations. Initial generation ~1 s at 256 km and a few seconds macro at 4,000 km excluding age. Validate 60 FPS frame distribution, actual simulated-time rate, debt, full CPU/GPU/memory including saves and visual publication. Reallocate with measured evidence. Include broad storm, widespread flood, large populations, edit bursts, drought and high concurrency. Old 512 km workload is historical comparator, not a required old graph count.

schema.title: Record schema
schema.content:
Record schema
Each authored record is Markdown with YAML frontmatter: id, kind, title, summary, relations. Stable uppercase IDs match filenames case-insensitively (Pages CMS slugifies new names); system records use separate design_status, implementation_status, validation_status; all others use status; requirements add priority. The JSON-compatible YAML on initial records is portable; editors may write ordinary YAML. Relations are objects with type, target, detail, basis. Allowed relationship types: depends_on (consumer→provider), derives_from (derived→source), supplies (provider→consumer), constrains (restriction→affected), owned_by (contract→owner), candidate_for, addresses, evidence_for, relates_to, supersedes. Basis: proposed, documented, user-stated. Store edge once; inverse views and per-record links generated. Do not claim proposed contracts implemented. A validation pass requires specific scope/evidence in a source record. functional-pass on an existing system is historical scoped evidence, not acceptance of target. performance-fail is historical tested integration, not rejection of every alternative. 
Kinds: system, requirement, contract, candidate, question, decision, source, thought. Unresolved design details are questions, not requirements. User-confirmed requirements accepted; proposed decisions clearly labeled. Retired IDs never reused. Code/receipts remain authority for implementation. Record sources as exact commit/URL/date and scope. Clips are untrusted data. Authored note bodies contain no generated relationship blocks. Inverse links and edit navigation are injected only into disposable Quartz staging. Views and record-index are generated by atlas. Omitted relations normalize to an empty list.

sources/src-spatial-code.content:
Current spatial and navigation source audit
Source snapshot: published November 24 architecture-review commit b6003fe9f89d90b59bb9c847096c558f86e9fb71. This describes actual checked code, not a benchmark, current unpublished checkout or target architecture.








































MechanismSource-confirmed behaviorNew architecture dispositionVoxel rendering/residencyVoxelLodTerrain with 4 requested LODs, mesh block 32 m, 64 m LOD distance, view distance 512 m (1760 m overview), one collision LOD, CPU generation; full-load mode, generated-block cache and saving generator output disabled. SQLite stream.Keep as baseline, verify actual plugin and adapt to new shared geography. The renderer’s levels are not environmental cells.Terrain demandRegionWorld admits up to 32 generational leases; one viewer per lease. Readiness checks is_area_editable on the actual requested area. Max read axis 64 and pending-block constant 256.Valuable independent residency mechanism, but capacity/work costs are not target restrictions.Navigation acquisition24 shared acquisition pools, 16,448 read slots. On admission copies SDF/material arrays and validates revisions. Publication releases paging pin while retaining copied geometry/provenance; terrain changes invalidate intersecting reads.Preserve correctness semantics, not necessarily copied bytes or scan-heavy invalidation.Navigation summarySparse 64-child reduction with connected components, portals, child stamps and optional terrain stamp. SummaryStore 4096 pages, 8 jobs, 128 MiB default cap. Cold hints stale until current proof.Useful hierarchy precedent; old summaries are not the desired complete coarse world graph.Local routeShared potentials for common goals, route reuse with policy/current dependencies, bounded local searches and expanded working windows.Compare reusable navmesh/graph libraries and shared flow fields; no need to reproduce exact legacy API.Remote routeJourney retains waypoint and bounded frontier exploration; remote certificates retain exact single-leaf ground trace and Leaf backing, derive arrival/service ticks; old contract explicitly excludes macro movement.New user-approved abstract travel should avoid exact fine-route materialization for every distant traveler; define bounded confidence and event checks.
Pinned source paths:

voxels_godot/world/regions/region_terrain_binding.gd
voxels_godot/world/regions/region_world.gd

Navigation types define 16 m leaf span, maximum level 10, ground/swim/air domains and historical 100,000 admission constant. These are current source constants, not new limits. Existing 1k and failed 100k measurements remain in SRC-NAV. Source inspection neither accepts nor rejects a replacement library.
Additional exact source inspection (25 November 2026)

Navigation key arithmetic uses checked floor division and 16 m leaf span scaled by 4 per axis; parent has 64 children. This is useful historical coordinate arithmetic but not a mandatory new hierarchy shape.
WorldDomain has 5,000,000 m maximum bounded half extent and 512,000 m maximum periodic half extent (1,024 km circumference), plus existing vertical bounds. Future 4,000 km wrap is not established.
Finite terrain geometry extracts per-column beds and crest/face relationships from SDF samples; a bounded patch method, not appropriate as a universal coarse-world preparation/update.
Pinned upstream Zylann generator, viewer and SQLite format inspected. Its native generator API has block input and optional series generation, and its repository already contains FastNoise2. Retain the useful voxel layer and qualify direct native geometry evaluation outside render/lease requests. Source inspection is not proof of the locally loaded binary or benchmark.

spatial-architecture-selection.title: Spatial architecture selection
spatial-architecture-selection.content:
Spatial architecture selection
Status: provisional engineering selection, source-qualified only (25 November 2026). Read accepted LOD requirement, world scale, authority, performance targets, terrain contract, navigation contract, water contract and prior qualification plan. No runtime implementation or performance acceptance.
1. Current implementation and replacement delta
The published source at b6003fe9f89d90b59bb9c847096c558f86e9fb71 has a working conceptual separation between Zylann rendering/residency and native navigation. It does not establish inexpensive coarse simulation of all distant effects. Pinned source audit.





























ExistingDispositionZylann VoxelLodTerrain, Clipbox, SQLite modified-block persistenceRetain provisionally, replace generator inputRegionWorld, explicit offscreen terrain leases and current edit stampsRetain semantics for exact local queries; no routine lease for coarse domainsNavigation 16 m leaf, 4x axis hierarchy, 64 child reduction; retained fine-derived certificatesKeep useful coordinate and revision logic; replace long-range full-detail proof requirementSDF floor/crest and legacy channel preparationReplace routine geographical derivation; exact local sampling only for dirty edits or exceptional interactionsCurrent native periodic max circumference 1,024 kmConfigurable bounded world pilot; qualify 4,000 km wrapping separately, never imply existing periodic implementation already scales
The pinned VoxelGenerator header supplies multithread-safe block generation with integer origin and LOD, optional series query, and a caller-owned voxel buffer. VoxelViewer allows visual/collision/data-notification needs to differ. SQLite stream format supports string and wider binary block keys. These already cover much of fine residency; avoid a new general-purpose voxel cache or per-colonist viewer. The pinned tree already includes FastNoise2; use existing graph/noise facilities where useful, do not import another noise package by default.
2. Select the simple structure for the pilot
Shared metric integer X/Z coordinates and local Y-up metre geometry, not a universal scene-tree hierarchy. One world identity/configuration. Existing checked 64-bit coordinates can be retained if verified; render relative to a local origin. Use a bounded rectangular world initially. Optional periodic topology must preserve actual extent, wrap intersections and seam identities; never silently pad the world. Arbitrary world dimensions use exact partial-edge area and boundary handling.
Logical addressing: a 16 km region/page, integer page coordinate and domain/field/level identifier; globally dense macro row-major arrays and a compact direct page directory. Region keys locate data, not ownership. Dense hot indices are not durable IDs. Use checked floor division for negative coordinates; local float coordinates only after origin subtraction. No pointer-rich octree for ordinary horizontal cells. Existing 16 m/32 m voxel blocks remain an independent 3D lattice. 250 m horizontal samples need not align to every voxel block. Where domains differ, exact overlap weights and feature contacts link them. Optional Morton sorting is a later measured optimization, not a prerequisite.
Pilot sizes (configurable, not hard requirements):















































RepresentationScale at 256 km baseline4,000 km candidateResidency / useMacro geological and geographic fields1 km (256²)approximately 4 km (1,000², or supported GeoGenesis sample count with explicit physical spacing)Whole world, cold formation and permanent compressed baselineRegional geographic/land refinement250 m1 km and 250 m only where meaningfulBounded page access and compact summary/latent recipe; actual land-water stores chosen by solverAdministrative page16 km16 kmDirect lookup; descriptor references optional field payloads and topology revisionsRiver/valley/lake/barrier featurePhysical coordinates and width/depth, independent of rasterSame principleCompact persistent network and sparse detailed profiles; latent detail if provable from recipeVolumetric terrain1 m base sample, adjustable; extra local fidelity if neededSameZylann request-driven generation and durable editsAtmosphere / soil / navigationIndependent field scales and intervalsIndependently qualifyMay share page/index coordinates without sharing representation
Do not require all 250 m pages to exist simultaneously. A region may have persistent coarse water, vegetation or human activity when its fine payload is absent. If an authoritative state has been refined or edited, keep its actual state/delta in memory or storage and ensure due events are applied; evict derived cache first, not physical consequences. Persist unresolved incoming amounts/time horizons until processed. No every-page catchup that silently stalls large active worlds. Base geometry and current edit layers are distinct; a coarse surface cannot be used as exact cave occupancy. A narrow stream must remain a feature even below the regional sample spacing.
Resource arithmetic, not measurements

4,000 km at 16 km gives 250 x 250 = 62,500 page descriptors. At an illustrative 32 B each: 1.91 MiB, before payloads.
4 km global samples: 1,000,000 cells. At 64 B/cell: 61.04 MiB.
1 km global samples: 16,000,000 cells. At 16 B/cell: 244.14 MiB; at 64 B/cell: 976.56 MiB.
250 m global: 256,000,000 cells, 15.26 GiB at 64 B/cell. A single 16 km page is 64² samples, 256 KiB at that stride; a 1024-page working set is 256 MiB. Not a mandated cache cap.
1 m global 2D footprint: 16 trillion samples, about 931 TiB at 64 B/sample, excluding vertical geometry.

Birth/age, derived geometry, scratch, active owners, caches, snapshots, edit journal and autosave must each be measured; a packed illustrative byte stride is not a memory estimate for GeoGenesis or any real solver. Bound total work with domain-specific cadence and active partitions. A storage page is not a simulation unit and must not force every owner to tick together.
3. Geographic data flow

Birth and age: run the accepted provisional GeoGenesis single-shot connected coarse simulation. Export final original surface, soil/sediment/geology, drainage area/receiver/order and refreshed climate/diagnostic runoff in explicit units. Use hydrology::route after age; lake fill depth is capacity diagnostic, not finite inventory. Preserve terminal basins; do not discard water at the root. Do not use the initial-only tiled path as if it aged regions. One-time field handoff; no second mutable formation world.
Coarse topology and boundaries: retain stable downstream contacts, closed-basin/spill identities, crossing positions and profiles, catchment extent and region revisions. Each region uses agreed physical boundary data derived once from the parent geography; arbitrary tile boundaries are not outlets. A region with no explicit drain is not automatically sea. Persist a resolved topology change when a dam or incision changes a crossing. Evaluate narrower drainage-aware refinement algorithms for tributaries before selecting them.
Detail realization: pilot the MIT Procedural World Generation donor. Its CPU channel and slope-conditioned detail routines accept supplied coarse/river inputs. Use or port only the reusable numerical pieces after license notices and source equivalence tests. Stable bed/bank geometry, not current water stage, constrains terrain. Sample globally keyed deterministic detail; bounded halo with canonical constraints; if drainage depends beyond halo, request/reconcile the affected parent/basin summary, not a new arbitrary border outlet. A render-dependent blend is not physical terrain authority. Additional source review found a deterministic local creek/trunk generator; its authoritative parent-outlet and closed-basin consistency remains open. See formation comparison.
Current geometry: Zylann renders/generates from the canonical region recipe and edit overlay. Coarse consumers derive geometry from the same recipe, feature profiles, and durable edits. Provide direct native block/batch evaluation without requesting scene nodes, voxel viewers or GPU readbacks on routine coarse queries. A mesh may approximate but cannot alter true bank/barrier or cave occupancy. Fine SDF acquisition is for local edits, exact interactions and exceptional corrections.
Process state: each solver owns its evolving quantities. Coarse surface stores retain distinct connected partitions, stage-volume and connections; channel geometry is a constraint, not water inventory. At promotion partition volume and constituent mass to children; at restriction aggregate accepted amounts; reconcile cross-boundary flux over the same interval. A camera movement alone must not change where water flows, how long travel takes or resource totals. Live erosion commits terrain deltas from actual forcing; do not recarve geometry each time a river rises.

A newly generated fine tributary may not contradict previously simulated parent runoff/route/basin outcomes. Its latent recipe or aggregate partition must constrain the prior simulation. If unresolved, label precision and require reconciliation before claiming exact topology, not a fictional fully resolved network. Closed depressions and narrow streams cannot be represented solely by average height. Large regional reroutes may require wider topology repair; local cost guarantee is limited to genuinely local edits.
4. Reuse selection













































ComponentRecommendationWhyGeoGenesisRetain provisional formation choiceConnected coarse geological age; flat fields, existing drainage kernel; no aged fine-tile refinerZylannRetain provisional fine terrain choiceExisting streaming/meshing/editing, no new volume engineProcedural World GenerationFirst refinement geometry donor to qualifyMIT, CPU routines exist for profiles, bounded carving and coarse-conditioned height; includes local trunk/creek generation; authoritative topology remains unqualifiedterrain-generator, flowing-terrainSecondary small donorsUseful isolated primitives, border and closed-basin limitationsMAIForge, hydrological construction trees, procedural planet river networksAlgorithm referencesClosely relevant regional outlet constraints; no permissive fully qualified implementation of complete refinementAMReX, OpenVDBNot the foundationScientific adaptive grids/volume storage add another layer; no need unless a particular qualified solver requires themlibmortonOptional after profilingNot needed for simple page lookup
Minimum custom code: field handoff/versioning, checked keys and page residency boundary, existing numerical-kernel adapter, feature-to-current-terrain contract, boundary reconciliation and dirty publication. Not a new custom renderer, sparse volume format, terrain erosion engine or navigation runtime. The outstanding tributary construction is real engineering risk, not hidden behind the term ‘hierarchy’.
5. First bounded qualification package
See spatial qualification. First run should be limited to formation plus geometry/refinement; no water runtime replacement, atmosphere, ECS migration or massive game build yet.

Confirm actual checkout, dependency pins and current Zylann generator extension boundary. Use the existing build tools and separate scratch lineage. Test negative coordinates, region boundaries, arbitrary edge extents and 4,000 km indexing without fine allocations.
Build the pinned GeoGenesis core with a minimal export, age one 256 km seed, refresh drainage, measure birth, age and field handoff separately. First use a small known two-region topological fixture to validate the donor, then use actual naturally generated terrain; do not present a manually placed creek fixture as a natural river generation pass.
Exercise the source donor CPU routines with a predeclared pair of adjacent regions, crossing channel profile, terminal depression, slope and spill control. Measure source baseline and native integration separately. Compare same sample positions from both evaluation orders, with neighbor absent/present, after eviction and after independent restart. Parent outlets, shared bank/bed profiles and basin identities must agree; no false drain or inserted water. For a roughly 1 m stream verify continuous feature geometry at finer local measurement resolution, and validate what the selected voxel/mesher resolution can actually represent.
Demonstrate an edit (dam or excavation) changes the relevant topology/summary and persists, including an offscreen edit. Track affected pages, requested voxel blocks and bytes. Invalidated data returns pending/coarse until its actual dependency is resolved; unrelated pages do not rebuild.
Measure complete small-world startup to macro-ready, feature-ready, and interactive terrain-ready. Then scale the macro/address/page directory probe to 4,000 km, not a fake fine-world test. Track inclusive CPU time, peak memory, generated/resident blocks and per-page latency. Compare images in the normal Godot host if integration reaches that point. Use historical 1 s 256 km macro/initial target and few seconds large-world macro separately from aging; record misses without altering physical clocks or excluding prep.

Pass criteria for qualification: no dense fine-world allocation; deterministic same-revision shared authoritative samples (within declared numeric precision), feature/closed-basin continuity, durable edit and bounded resident work independent of camera; agreed geometric error thresholds frozen before tests; actual measured cost and rendered quality. Failure returns to candidate research, not a mandate to build an entire new terrain engine. Broad storm, conservative transfers and 800 km travel are the subsequent consumer gates, not proven by the spatial fixture.
Open: Q-GRID exact domain resolutions; Q-REFINE fine tributary/saddle construction and topology summaries; hydraulic and atmosphere algorithm selection. This record selects a structure and a first permissive refinement donor to test, not finished solver implementation.
Formation review supplement
The spatial structure remains proposed unchanged. The subsequent formation comparison supersedes the earlier assumption that only GeoGenesis should be evaluated for birth. Test Procedural World Generation as a full alternative before committing to the source of the macro fields. The existing GeoGenesis-only fixture remains a comparison path, not a mandate.

spatial-qualification.title: Spatial qualification plan
spatial-qualification.content:
Spatial qualification plan
Status: proposed research and implementation qualification sequence. No runtime execution authorized. Read DEC-SPATIAL-PILOT, Q-GRID, Q-REFINE and REQ-BUDGET.
A. Shared field and topology contract
For every candidate record: upstream commit/license/dependencies, actual input/output storage, ownership, units, supported topology, required initialization, per-step/repair complexity, clock, thread count, CPU/GPU traffic, scratch, snapshot and persistence cost. Identify whether an implementation or only a paper is available. Do not invent a custom solver merely because an algorithm has a familiar name.
A region key identifies world, coordinate and level, not authority. Use integer/double coordinates for giant worlds with local render transforms. Fields specify physical extent, sample convention, units, geometry/version, time interval and exact/coarse/pending/stale state. Wrapping is an explicit boundary policy.
B. Formation/refinement gate

Run GeoGenesis single-shot coarse age at 256² or 512²; export final original bed, fresh climate/receivers, material and soil descriptors, and units. Time generation, age and export separately.
Compare reusable drainage-aware refinement: coarse-to-fine feature constraints or regional evolution. Use two adjacent regions and a shared boundary crossing, one narrow creek, two distinct basins and a known spill threshold. Test with deliberately shifted fine relief, alternate generation orders, eviction and reload. Geometry and topology must agree; a nicer image alone fails.
Preserve upstream/outlet IDs and boundary elevation/profile; do not force every depression to drain. Exclude fake filled water depth from initial mass. Capture actual Godot terrain from the same source when the integration is authorized.
Scale probe macro 4,000 km without allocating all 250 m or metre geometry. Measure total bytes, source generation, topology preparation, and initial interactive readiness separately. Reject hidden global fine preprocessing.

C. Broad flood gate
A 100 x 100 km island is 160,000 cells at 250 m, 10,000 at 1 km, versus 10 billion at metre spacing. Select actual subgrid transport methods and compare coarse and finer reference results for a severe storm covering the island. Include a protected lowland behind a levee, closed lake, dam/diversion, downstream flooding, recession, soil infiltration and evaporation. No global promotion to fine solver. Quantify mass error, flood extent, duration, water level and arrival error independently; define acceptable numerical tolerances before the test. Report fine residency high-water mark and work during peak flood. An island-wide wetness overlay is not a hydraulic pass.
D. Cross-system authority gate
Demonstrate one interval of actual evaporation -> vapor advection -> condensation -> precipitation -> land runoff -> finite water storage -> actual erosion forcing. Add sparse basic contamination and representative non-water inventory when qualifying liquid transport. No double crediting water or material. Show how vegetation consumes soil moisture and weather, and how vegetation feedback changes ET and erosion resistance. Validate direction and units of current/wind fields. Save/reload pending intervals and offscreen edits.
E. Navigation/entity gate
Plan a route across 800 km without loading a continuous metre-scale corridor. Use region/portal summaries; refinement is for uncertain crossings and consequential local motion, not all distant traversals. Include a bridge or pass that closes from flooding and a cave/multifloor route. Unknown/pending/stale never equals proven blocked or exact valid. Compare travel time and arrival to a smaller fine reference, and test batched repeated work cycles with finite supplies. Evaluate a common ECS plus prebuilt local navigation/crowd candidates in 1k, 10k, 100k mixed active populations; no empty-entity benchmark.
Decision checkpoints

































QuestionDecision evidence requiredQ-REFINELicensed reusable method, deterministic seam, narrow-stream/lake geometry and actual startup costQ-GRIDDomain resolution and ownership table with complete memory/work measurements, large-world scalingQ-FLOODSigned transport law, finite storage, protected lowland and whole-island stormQ-ATMOSActual wind/moisture transport, finite precipitation cycle and severe-weather costQ-EROSIONReusable kernel with actual runtime flux/material input, bounded terrain editsQ-NAVLong-distance planning without full fine residency, dynamic hazards, crowd and refinement tests
The priority is to close formation/geometry contracts and hydraulic/atmospheric selection in parallel with the smallest cross-domain proofs, not complete every later feature now. Retain historical failures and distinguish source facts, theoretical estimates, small tests and production acceptance.

systems/sys-lod.title: Spatial hierarchy and residency
systems/sys-lod.content:
Spatial hierarchy and residency
Logical world always exists. Coarse authoritative stores and persistent feature summaries may be resident globally; fine procedural blocks are generated/read on demand, edited blocks durable. Separate terrain data residency, rendering LOD, simulation LOD, navigation abstraction and entity detail. A coarse cell need not represent a single river or traversable passage. Use stable coordinates, revision-stamped summaries and bounded caches. Promotion/restriction preserves volume, material, population identity and causal events; no duplicated owner. Exact spatial scales/tiling open, not fixed 1 km or 250 m.
Verified published implementation boundary
Current spatial source audit distinguishes existing camera-independent leases, fine navigation copies, summary residency and the exact remote-segment restriction. The spatial pilot is the proposed replacement qualification, not an implementation claim.

Existing native hierarchical/shared routes and local certificates had bounded 1k acceptance, not massive scale qualification. systems/sys-refine.title: Geographic refinement and drainage
systems/sys-refine.content:
Geographic refinement and drainage
Missing algorithm. Fine regions and features must agree across tile boundaries, preserve river connectivity and downhill grades, lake boundaries, and watershed structure; not noise added independently. A narrow creek is a persistent subgrid feature, not averaged away. Investigate reusable procedural hydrology and multiresolution erosion; share deterministic generator and relevant feature geometry with terrain and hydraulic derivation. No resurrection of LandscapeChannels.
Candidate narrowed
The first permissive geometry donor is Procedural World Generation; the remaining topology question is explicitly open. See spatial architecture selection. No implementation status change.
Updated research boundary
Procedural World Generation’s creekGen is a concrete deterministic trunk and tributary-growth donor, not yet an authoritative refined drainage network. Qualify it with a fixed geometry callback, parent outlet and basin consistency, and residency-independent results. The remaining work is integration and verification, not automatically writing a tributary engine from scratch. See formation comparison.

Select actual reusable numerical method; a graph is not a solver. Surface hydraulic queries feed gameplay and erosion; candidate clocks must not disguise physical time.

systems/sys-time.title: Time, settings and clocks
systems/sys-time.content:
Time, settings and clocks
Store settings in validated versioned configuration with defaults and permitted ranges. World day 600 s at 1x, year 60 days default. No universal fixed step. Explicit seconds, game calendar, geological years and solver intervals; track elapsed work and pending events. No compressed physical clock to pass performance. Config changes requiring regeneration or incompatible state must be explicit.

systems/sys-world.title: World formation
systems/sys-world.content:
World formation
Target: varied continents/islands, mountains, valleys, hills, cliffs, plateaus, coastlines, climate zones and strata. GeoGenesis provisional for initial coarse formation. Export final fields once to shared geography; use deterministic world seed/config. Initial macro generation and aging separately timed. No claim full volumetric caves or ore bodies supplied by a 2D formation grid. Current documented native LandscapeFormation is a replacement subject, not target architecture.

workflow.title: Working with the brain
workflow.content:
Working with the brain

Read the home, record-index.json and relevant requirements, contracts, systems and evidence. Follow typed edges in both directions.
Capture a thought, proposed requirement or question. Use a permanent uppercase ID such as THO-FLOOD-IDEA. Filenames may match case-insensitively. Do not rename existing IDs.
Pages CMS edits authored Markdown and metadata in eight collections. Generated connections are injected into the Quartz stage, never into the editor body. Do not manually edit generated views or index.
On the dedicated brain branch, validated edits trigger an automatic refresh. Agents can run python docs/brain/tools/atlas.py --write and --check; run python docs/brain/tools/test_brain.py for editor payload checks. A failed validation requires correcting the record, not bypassing the checks.
Distinguish user intent, proposal, implementation and measured validation. Capture source/version/license, API, performance/units and limitations. No engine changes follow from note edits. Validated Brain branch edits rebuild the user-approved public GitHub Pages documentation and publish only generated files to caleb-var/breachborn-brain/main/docs. All authoring stays in the private game repository; never edit the public mirror. All authored content including inbox is public by default; keep confidential notes outside content/.

Open Pages CMS after account authorization. GitHub Markdown editing remains available.
